units: Lev. R. s. 2 בא ואראך כבודי ובית שְׁכִינָתִי וכ׳ (not ביתי; some ed. שכונתי) come, and I will show thee my honor and the house of my residence without thy mother; Yalk. Ez. 340 כבודי ובית שבניתי לאמך (corr. acc.). Lev. R. l. c. כלום פיחת כבודי ושכינתי has my honor or my royalty suffered (through thy mother’s absence)?; Yalk. l. c. כבודי או בית שבניתי לכם (corr. acc.).—Esp. Shechinah, Divine Presence, holy inspiration (v.

<cite ref="Yoma 9b:18">Yoma 9ᵇ</cite> sq. <he>אי נמי סליקו … לא הוה שריא ש׳ … אין הש׳ שורה וכ׳</he> even if all Jews had returned in Ezra’s days, the Sh. would not have dwelt in the second Temple, for it is written (<cite ref="Genesis 9:27">Gen. IX, 27</cite>) …; the Sh. dwells only in the tents of Shem; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 36:8">Gen. R. s. 36</cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 6a:10">Ber. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>לשלשה … שש׳ עמהם</he> that when three sit as judges, the Sh. is with them.
<cite ref="Shabbat 12b:3">Sabb. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ למעלה וכ׳</he> the Sh. dwells over the headside of the sick man’s bed.
<cite ref="Megillah 29a:4">Meg. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>בכל מקום שגלו ש׳ עמהן</he> whithersoever they were exiled, the Sh. went with them.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 25a:10">B. Bath. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ בכל מקום</he> the Sh. Is everywhere (you may face any region in prayer).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 31a:18">R. Hash. 31ᵃ</cite>; a. fr. (also in Chald. diction).
